title: technical defect lesson — produced code without type annotations
rationale: Tier-1 explicit correction of an attributable skill's output: it wrote functions with no type hints in a typed codebase. A genuine technical-compliance defect -> raise the gate. The case grades the synthesized lesson: it must read as a technical/code defect and say concretely what to change.

assertions.rubric: Grade the `Lesson:` line of the gate. PASS only if it: (1) reads clearly as a TECHNICAL / code defect — about the technical correctness of what the skill produced; (2) names the concrete problem: the generated functions were missing type annotations / type hints; (3) states what correct looks like in actionable terms (the skill should add type annotations / follow the codebase's typing requirement); (4) is generalizable and de-identified. FAIL if it is vague, reads as a generic behavioral note with no technical specifics, or omits the corrective ('what correct looks like').

prompt:

- The UserPromptSubmit primer flagged correction language in the user's latest message.

The user's latest message at this turn boundary is:

Apply the feedback-detector skill's full procedure to THIS turn boundary now and produce exactly the output the skill dictates. Treat the explicit correction of the skill's untyped output as the Tier-1 signal. Do not ask me clarifying questions first; act on the primed turn state.
